extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for reviewers evaluating ICLR 2021 submissions, covering what to look for in papers, how to write reviews, procedural duties (bidding, discussion, CoE reporting), and how to provide final recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely and substantive reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Your reviews are timely and substantive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Meet the listed deadlines (create profile, bid, write review, participate in discussion, provide final recommendation). Timeliness includes submitting initial reviews during the review window and being active during the discussion phase.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adherence to Code of Ethics and Code of Conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: You must adhere to our Code of Ethics in your role as a reviewer. You must also adhere to our Code of Conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Read the CoE before reviewing. Complete a CoE report for each paper (simple form with two questions). Flag potential CoE violations when submitting the CoE report; AC/PC/ethics board will resolve cases. For other violations (plagiarism, double submission, formatting) contact AC/PC via official comment with appropriate readership restrictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall aim: value and contribution
rubrics_metrics.description: A review aims to determine whether a submission will bring sufficient value to the community and contribute new knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this as the high-level criterion when recommending Accept vs Reject: value to ICLR community and contribution of new, relevant, impactful knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thorough reading and literature awareness
rubrics_metrics.description: Carefully read through the entire paper, and look up any related work and citations that will help you comprehensively evaluate it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give yourself sufficient time. Supplementary material is not necessary to read but can often answer questions; consider looking there before asking authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider the work's objective
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess the objective of the work: is the goal to address a known application/problem, draw attention to a new problem/application, or introduce/explain a new theoretical finding (or a combination)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different objectives require different considerations about potential value and impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity of presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the submission clear?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mention clarity as a strong/weak point. Identify confusing sections and typos; suggest clarifications. Be positive and generous in the summary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical correctness
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the submission technically correct?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify correctness of theoretical claims, proofs, and algorithmic descriptions. Point out errors or gaps in reasoning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental rigor
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the experiments rigorous?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess experimental design, baselines, hyperparameter tuning, ablation studies, statistical validity, breadth of datasets/tasks. Ask for limited-scope experiments if they help validate existing claims; new experiments should not significantly change the content of the submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproducibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the results reproducible?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check whether methods, hyperparameters, and data splits are described; consider supplementary material and code availability. Requesting reproducibility artifacts is reasonable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty / contribution of new findings
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the submission present novel findings (e.g., theoretical, algorithmic, etc.)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the idea is new and non-trivial; consider whether it meaningfully advances the field even if it is not state-of-the-art on benchmarks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motivation and placement in literature
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the approach well motivated, including being well-placed in the literature?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess how authors situate their work relative to prior work and whether the motivation justifies the approach. Consider contemporaneous work policy: papers published within two months before deadline may be excused from comparison.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support of claims by evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the paper support its claims? This includes determining if results, whether theoretical or empirical, are correct and scientifically rigorous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for convincing experiments, proofs, or analyses that back claims. If claims are not supported, list specific missing analyses or evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bias awareness and open-mindedness
rubrics_metrics.description: Be mindful of potential biases and try to be open-minded about the value and interest a paper can hold for the entire ICLR community, even if it may not be very interesting for you.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid personal preference bias; consider broader community relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three key questions to answer
rubrics_metrics.description: Answer three key questions to make a recommendation: (1) What is the specific question/problem tackled? (2) Is the approach well motivated and well-placed in the literature? (3) Does the paper support the claims (results correct and rigorous)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these answers to form your Accept/Reject recommendation; be explicit in addressing each.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial review structure and content
rubrics_metrics.description: Organize the initial review to include: summary of claimed contributions; list of strong and weak points; clear recommendation with 1–2 key reasons; supporting arguments; questions for authors; additional feedback to improve the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be positive and generous in the summary. Make clear which feedback is aimed at improvement and which affects the decision. Provide concise rationale for recommendation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide specific, constructive feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide additional feedback with the aim to improve the paper; make clear these points are to help and not necessarily part of your decision assessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give actionable suggestions (e.g., additional experiments, clarifications, analyses) and point out minor issues (typos, notation) separately from major concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completing the CoE report for each paper
rubrics_metrics.description: ICLR requires reviewers to complete a Code of Ethics report for each paper assigned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report asks whether there is a potential CoE violation and if so to explain why. Submit the CoE report immediately after completing your initial review; the button appears after submitting the review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Active engagement in discussion phase
rubrics_metrics.description: During the discussion phase, reviewers, authors and area chairs engage in asynchronous discussion and authors are allowed to revise submissions; reviewers must be actively engaged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use discussion to clarify points, request limited additional experiments or clarifications, and re-evaluate in light of author responses. Be timely and civil in discussions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Update final recommendation after discussion
rubrics_metrics.description: Update your review and final recommendation taking into account new information collected during the discussion phase and any revisions to the submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain openness to changing your initial recommendation either more positive or more negative, and justify any change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate requests for additional experiments
rubrics_metrics.description: You can ask for additional experiments, but new experiments should not significantly change the content of the submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests should be limited in scope and serve to more thoroughly validate existing results rather than require a major rewrite or new direction.

rubrics_metrics.name: State on state-of-the-art (SOTA) results
rubrics_metrics.description: A lack of state-of-the-art results does not by itself constitute grounds for rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate submissions on whether they convincingly demonstrate new, relevant, impactful knowledge; SOTA is neither necessary nor sufficient alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling policy/formatting/plagiarism concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: To discuss or flag other policy violations (e.g., plagiarism, double submission, paper length, formatting), contact either the AC or the PC as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use an official comment with appropriate readership restrictions or contact chairs directly; flag CoE separately through CoE report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expectation for citing contemporaneous work
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are considered excused from comparing to papers published within the last two months before the full paper deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Since deadline is Oct 2, papers published on or after Aug 2, 2020 are not required to be compared. Authors are encouraged to cite relevant work but may be excused for not knowing very recent non-peer-reviewed or late papers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid and report conflicts of interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid being assigned papers that present a conflict of interest by updating your OpenReview profile (co-authors, past and current institutions, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you see a COI while bidding, bid 'Very Low'. If assigned a paper that presents a COI, contact program chairs immediately to have it re-assigned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review examples and formatting expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Model reviews show a clear summary, explicit pros and cons, questions for authors, and final decision rationale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use example reviews as templates for clarity and structure; include concise typos/minor comments separately and clearly label post-rebuttal updates if you change your stance.
